Messier per-benchmark summary. Rows grouped by benchmark group (§4); verifier and aggregation taxonomies defined in §3. The Verifiers column counts per-criterion rows for multi-verifier tasks and the task itself otherwise. Outcomes counts per-trial scoring events, with one entry per criterion for multi-verifier tasks. HarveyAI-Lab, MedAgentBench, DABStep, QCircuitBench, ReplicationBench, and ScienceAgentBench were collected via Harbor under a uniform five-agent OpenHands grid. Total agents is the union across benchmarks.

Composition and frontier analysis. Panels summarize the corpus across the dimensions defined in §3: (a) tasks by benchmark group, (b) action space, (c) environment state, (d) aggregation rule, and (e) verifier type. Counts in (b)–(e) are on a log scale. Panel (f) tracks frontier pass rate by release quarter and benchmark group, with dumbbell markers connecting each group’s first and final observed quarter.

Capability orderings from Messier vs. Epoch’s ECI. Each panel plots Messier-fit per-agent θ\theta (logit scale) against Epoch’s published ECI for the matched subset, with Spearman ρ\rho, 95% bootstrap CI over 1000 resamples, pairwise concordance, and matched-agent count. The General panel uses Epoch’s overall ECI (n=75n=75); Coding uses SWE-ECI (n=59n=59); Math uses Math-ECI (n=63n=63). A 1PL fit on Messier alone aligns with Epoch’s orderings without any new evaluation campaign.

Counterfactual aggregation on benchmarks with per-criterion outcomes. We rescore the same trials under three alternative rules: all-pass (the official rule), soft (mean fraction of criteria passed), and ≥50%\geq 50\% (majority pass). Near-pass is the fraction of trials that fail all-pass but pass at least 80%80\% of criteria. The last column reports the Spearman rank correlation across agents between their mean all-pass and mean soft scores: ρ=1\rho=1 would mean the two rules preserve agent ordering; lower values indicate the rules reorder agents.

Difficulty prediction across two targets and two input configurations. Targets: raw IRT difficulty β\beta and within-benchmark zz-scored β\beta. Inputs: task = raw instruction text; all = concatenation of task, environment, and action descriptions plus gold answer. The baseline predicts the training-fold benchmark mean. Entries report Spearman ρ\rho under 5-fold cross-validation, mean ±\pm std across folds. N=10,406N=10{,}406 tasks.

Per-benchmark sources and upstream license/access status. Group ordering follows Table 2. aux. marks secondary releases used to cross-reference or fill per-task gaps under normalized identifiers. The license/status column reports the terms identified for the cited upstream source; it does not define the license of Messier as a whole.
